memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"And God spoke all these words: 'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of
Egypt, out of the land of slavery.'" - Ex 20:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before a single command, God introduces Himself. And notice how He does it.

Not "I am the Almighty who made the heavens," though He is. Not "I am the God
who will punish you if you disobey." He says: I am the one who brought you out of
slavery.

This sentence is the foundation of everything that follows. The Ten Commandments
do not begin with a demand. They begin with a rescue that has already happened.

That order changes what the commandments are. They are not a ladder to climb
toward God's acceptance. They are the shape of life for a people who have already
been claimed and freed. God did not say "keep these and I will save you." He
said, in effect, "I have saved you; now here is how the rescued live."

Get this wrong and the whole Bible tilts. Many people carry a sense that God is
essentially a rule-giver whose approval must be earned. Israel met Him as a
rescuer first.

Paul makes the same point in a different key: "It is for freedom that Christ has
set us free" (Gal 5:1). Free first, then live accordingly.

Notice too the word "your." I am the LORD your God. This is relationship before
regulation.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you experience God primarily as a rescuer or as a rule-giver?
2. What difference does it make that the commandments come after the exodus?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You rescued me before You asked anything of me. Let my
obedience flow from gratitude, not fear. Amen.
